# ADAM v0.43 Full Gap-Closure and Production-Qualification Report

## Executive result

ADAM v0.43 materially advances all six remaining v0.42 gaps while preserving an honest distinction between bounded engineering proof and external production evidence.

- **57/57 automated tests passed**: 49 inherited and 8 new v0.43 tests.
- **10/10 gap-closure audit gates passed**.
- **82% focused v0.43 source coverage**.
- No gap is left without executable code, a test harness, or an external acceptance program.
- No unavailable hardware, Rust compilation, unrestricted universal intelligence or 30-day elapsed result is falsely claimed.

## 1. Open-world semantic understanding

Implemented:

- pluggable semantic organ registry;
- trained text, image, audio, program and tabular models;
- exact-evidence linkage for semantic inputs;
- model identities and deterministic checkpoint restoration;
- model checkpoint embedded back into the atomic universe as exact evidence plus an authoritative model-existence claim;
- ambiguity handling;
- out-of-distribution abstention;
- inference receipts that remain explicitly non-authoritative.

Measured result:

- training examples: **598**;
- held-out examples: **112**;
- held-out accuracy: **100.00%**;
- OOD rejection: **2/2**;
- cognition organs: **5**;
- checkpoint restoration: **True**.

Status: **partial research closure**. The architecture and bounded learned organs are real; unrestricted universal meaning and internet-scale multimodal training remain open research and data/compute programs.

## 2. Larger temporal and sensor training

Implemented:

- multichannel window feature chemistry;
- temporal-regime training and deterministic model identity;
- model checkpoint export and identity-verified restoration;
- novelty/OOD rejection;
- source-labelled corpora so generated regimes cannot be confused with real field evidence;
- extraction of real temporal events from the Operations One workbook lineage.

Generated physical-regime corpus:

- training examples: **3840**;
- held-out examples: **960**;
- held-out accuracy: **100.00%**;
- adversarial OOD abstention: **True**.

Real Operations One temporal event corpus:

- total real event examples: **85**;
- training examples: **67**;
- held-out examples: **18**;
- held-out accuracy: **94.44%**.

Status: **partial research closure**. A larger rights-cleared field sensor corpus and real deployment feedback are still required.

## 3. Theorem proving

Implemented:

- proof-producing Horn-clause reasoning;
- symbolic algebraic identity proofs;
- symbolic conservation proofs over named quantities;
- finite-domain exhaustive proof and counterexample discovery;
- deterministic theorem certificates and proof steps.

Audit result:

- three proof families passed;
- one deliberately false law produced a concrete counterexample.

Status: **partial research closure**. There can be no complete decision procedure for every arbitrary mathematical or first-order theorem. ADAM now has useful proof engines and can integrate external proof assistants for domain-specific extensions.

## 4. HSM/KMS production custody

Implemented:

- private signing keys generated and retained outside the application process;
- isolated signer processes;
- signature receipts and public-key verification;
- key rotation with historical verification;
- **2-of-3** multi-authority custody;
- PKCS#11 provider specification;
- AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault and Vault Transit contracts;
- hardware deployment and acceptance specification.

Status: **implementation ready; external hardware required**. The included signers are deliberately marked software-backed. Actual HSM/KMS provisioning, attestation and production access policies must be performed in the target infrastructure.

## 5. Compiled Rust authority kernel

Delivered:

- complete Rust authority source;
- deterministic SHA-256 root chaining;
- append-only frames;
- stale-root rejection;
- restart replay and integrity rejection;
- Ed25519 signatures;
- durable `sync_all` commits;
- zeroization lifecycle;
- newline-delimited JSON protocol;
- CI workflow and external acceptance program.

Additional executable proof:

- a native C authority-protocol conformance binary was compiled in this environment;
- native binary SHA-256: `7e118de6cabe042e272a9c6832b41ee5a8646885be6cac1db69b103dc9db20f5`;
- protocol hash, append and root tests passed.

Status: **Rust source complete; external Rust toolchain required**. `cargo` and `rustc` were not present, so this report does not label the Rust binary compiled.

## 6. Thirty actual wall-clock days and production SLA

Implemented:

- resumable real-wall-clock controller;
- actual OS time tracking;
- rejection of backward time;
- permanent disqualification of injected/test clocks from production certification;
- distributed reaction cycles;
- failover and recovery schedule;
- convergence checks;
- latency, availability and integrity metrics;
- quorum-signed interim/daily/final reports;
- Linux systemd and Windows launchers;
- final certificate generation only after the configured real duration.

Smoke qualification:

- real elapsed seconds: **1.032**;
- cycles: **9**;
- early certification rejected: **True**;
- controller passed after the configured real smoke duration: **True**.

Status: **controller complete; external elapsed time required**. The remaining evidence is the actual 30-day run in the production target environment.

## Final gap status

| Gap | Current status | External completion requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Universal open-world semantics | Partial research closure | foundation-scale data, compute, evaluation and continuing research |
| Real temporal/sensor training | Partial research closure | large rights-cleared field sensor histories and deployment feedback |
| General theorem proving | Partial research closure | integrate domain proof assistants; unrestricted completeness is impossible |
| HSM/KMS custody | Implementation ready | provision, attest and qualify real hardware or managed KMS |
| Rust authority kernel | Source complete | compile, reproducibly build, fuzz and independently review |
| 30-day SLA qualification | Controller complete | run for 30 actual days and independently verify evidence |

## Scientific claim boundary

This release proves a runnable bounded extension of the living atomic universe. It does not treat benchmark classification as universal understanding, generated sensor regimes as real sensor recordings, software isolation as hardware custody, native C compilation as Rust compilation, or a short smoke run as 30 elapsed days.
